known_facts_book1: A town where the houses are made of bread and crackers and every man, woman and child is made of buns and bread.
Its people, alarmed at ravenous human visitors, debate whether to admit Dorothy for fear of being eaten.
Dorothy visits it while lost, with Toto and Billina.
Mr. Bunn and Mrs. Over (President of the Bunbury Breakfast) are among its leading citizens.
Dorothy breakfasts on a bread wheelbarrow and a bread piano, and Billina eats the crumbs, before being driven out.

known_relations_book1.Dorothy: The lost visitor whom the bread people fear as an eater.
known_relations_book1.Mr. Bunn: A leading bun citizen of the town.

not_in_this_book: Bunbury is ruled by a King

known_facts_book1: A city of dressed-up rabbits enclosed by a high marble wall, built and protected by Glinda the Good.
No one may enter without a letter of introduction from Ozma or Glinda, checked by the Keeper of the Wicket.
Dorothy grows smaller and smaller to pass through its tiny door, ending up no taller than a rabbit.
Is ruled by a Rabbit King who whines and weeps and wants to leave his throne for a wild life.
Dorothy lunches with the King and persuades him to be content and stay, threatening to tell Glinda.

known_relations_book1.Glinda: The Sorceress who built and protects the city.
known_relations_book1.Dorothy: The visitor who cheers up its unhappy Rabbit King.

not_in_this_book: Bunnybury is a town of bread people

hallucination_signals: Bunnybury is ruled by King Kleaver

known_facts_book1: The people of the town of Fuddlecumjig, made of many small jigsaw-puzzle pieces.
They scatter themselves into heaps of pieces when strangers approach and must be put back together like a picture puzzle.
The wagon party matches together the cook, the Lord High Chigglewitz and Grandmother Gnit, who then host a dinner.
The Lord High Chigglewitz, first name Larry, is the chief personage of the town.

known_relations_book1.Grandmother Gnit: A Fuddle whom the visitors piece together.
known_relations_book1.Dorothy: One of the visitors who reassembles the scattered Fuddles.

not_in_this_book: the Fuddles are made of bread

known_facts_book1: A kingdom of living kitchen utensils, ruled by King Kleaver, hidden off any path in the forest.
Its Spoon Brigade, spoons carrying swords and muskets, capture Dorothy, Toto and Billina.
Dorothy is brought before King Kleaver and the utensils debate what to do with the prisoners.
Dorothy laughs off the danger and leaves without harm, finding no food she can eat there.

known_relations_book1.Dorothy: The prisoner captured by the Spoon Brigade.

known_facts_book1: A town whose people, the Rigmaroles, speak in endless long-winded speeches using many words but saying little.
A boy and a woman there answer simple questions with streams of words that never seem to end.
The wagon party gives up and moves on rather than wait for the Rigmaroles to finish.
People who become too long-winded elsewhere in Oz are sent to live in Rigmarole Town.

known_relations_book1.the Wizard: Who guides the party there and laughs at the endless talk.
known_relations_book1.Dorothy: A visitor who loses track of what the Rigmaroles are saying.

not_in_this_book: the Rigmaroles are made of bread

hallucination_signals: the bread people of Rigmarole Town
